title: HOUSING AND INFRASTRUCTURE
text:
HOUSING AND INFRASTRUCTURE

Objectives:
1. Learn the importance of good housing to dairy animals
2. Familiarize the criteria in area selection for dairy farm and points to consider in housing establishment.
3. Acquaint with dairy infrastructure, materials used in the construction and best practices in cow comfort.
4. Familiarize the equipment and support facilities needed in dairy operations.

Why provide a good housing for dairy cattle?
1. to protect the animals from extreme weather conditions.
2. for easy administration of technical services.
3. ease in doing daily farm activities like milking, cleaning and feeding.

What are the basic considerations for area selection?
1. Housing area per animal.
CLASS AND AGE | Shed or Barn Floor Area( sq. meter/animal)
Calves (up to 3 months) | 1
Calves (3-6 months) | 2
Calves (7 months – 1 year) | 3
Yearlings(1-2 years) | 4
Heifer/Steer(2-3 years) | 5
Milking and dry cows | 6
Pregnant cows | 10

2. Orientation of the farm.
[Diagram showing Farm building situated in an east-west orientation with sun paths for Summer and Winter]
Farm building should be situated in a east-west orientation

facts: Learning objectives of the module include understanding the importance of housing, criteria for area selection and housing establishment, dairy infrastructure and cow comfort materials/practices, and equipment/support facilities.
Providing good housing protects dairy cattle from extreme weather conditions.
Good housing facilitates easy administration of technical services.
Good housing provides ease in executing daily farm activities such as milking, cleaning, and feeding.
The required shed or barn floor area for calves up to 3 months old is 1 sq. meter per animal.
The required shed or barn floor area for calves aged 3 to 6 months is 2 sq. meters per animal.
The required shed or barn floor area for calves aged 7 months to 1 year is 3 sq. meters per animal.
The required shed or barn floor area for yearlings (1 to 2 years) is 4 sq. meters per animal.
The required shed or barn floor area for heifers or steers (2 to 3 years) is 5 sq. meters per animal.
The required shed or barn floor area for milking and dry cows is 6 sq. meters per animal.
The required shed or barn floor area for pregnant cows is 10 sq. meters per animal.
Farm buildings should be situated in an east-west orientation to optimize exposure to the sun during summer and winter.
